subject: history

moments.title: Mountbatten's deadline
moments.body: Clement Attlee announces British withdrawal by June 1948. Mountbatten arrives in March 1947 and brings the date forward to 15 August. Cyril Radcliffe is given five weeks to draw the border between India and Pakistan, having never visited the subcontinent.
moments.takeaway: Speed was Mountbatten's signature strategy. It also made the violence worse — communities had weeks, not months, to decide.

moments.title: Independence and violence
moments.who: Nehru, Jinnah, communities across Punjab and Bengal
moments.body: 14-15 August 1947: Pakistan and India become independent. Around 15 million people are displaced — the largest migration in human history. Estimated deaths in communal violence: 200,000 to 2 million. Punjab is split; Bengal is split; the princely states must choose sides. Kashmir's accession is contested.

quote.text: Long years ago we made a tryst with destiny.
quote.attrib: Jawaharlal Nehru, 'Tryst with Destiny' speech, midnight 14-15 August 1947

moments.takeaway: Mahatma Gandhi did not attend the independence celebrations. He was in Calcutta trying to stop communal violence. He was assassinated on 30 January 1948.

moments.title: First Kashmir war
moments.body: October 1947: Pakistani-backed tribal forces invade Kashmir. Maharaja Hari Singh accedes to India. War follows; a UN ceasefire holds from 1 January 1949 along the Line of Control. The dispute is unresolved.
moments.takeaway: Three full wars (1947-48, 1965, 1999) and continuous tension have followed. Both states became nuclear powers in 1998.

now.title: The unfinished partition
now.body: 1947 created two of the world's largest nations and a refugee experience that still shapes Indian, Pakistani and Bangladeshi political identity. Bangladesh seceded from Pakistan in 1971 after another war and another genocide. The Citizenship Amendment Act (India, 2019), the Hindutva movement, and Kashmir's revoked autonomy (2019) extend partition's unfinished business.
now.open_questions: Could partition have been avoided? Yasmin Khan's 'The Great Partition' (2007) shows the rushed implementation was not preordained. Ayesha Jalal has argued Jinnah's demand for Pakistan was originally a bargaining position.

reflection: Decolonisation can be catastrophic for those decolonised. 1947 is a warning about the cost of rushed political settlements imposed on populations who have to live their consequences.
